title: Publish Runtime LTS baseline benchmark set + stabilize dataset/versioning
author: Allison Grant
description:
Context: For Runtime LTS we need performance results that are comparable across patch releases (e.g. runtime-1.20-lts.0 -> lts.1 -> lts.2). Today our perf jobs pull “latest” datasets/prompt sets and a few configs drift over time (prompt ordering, tokenizer rev, sampling seeds, dataset sharding), which makes p95/p99 deltas hard to trust and makes audit evidence painful.

This PR publishes a versioned, pinned "LTS baseline" benchmark set (v1) and adds explicit dataset + harness versioning so LTS perf-gates can reference immutable inputs.

What’s in this PR:
- Add LTS baseline benchmark suite definition: `suites/runtime_lts_baseline_v1.yaml` (models, seq-lens, batch profiles, metrics).
- Introduce dataset manifests with immutable content hashes: `datasets/manifests/*.jsonl` (one manifest per dataset slice) and a top-level `datasets/lts_baseline_v1.lock` containing SHA256s.
- Stabilize dataset versioning and download paths: all dataset fetches now go through `bench datasets fetch --lockfile ...` and verify checksums.
- Freeze prompt set ordering and sampling seeds for LTS suite runs (seed pinned in suite yaml; per-workload seed in manifest).
- Add "harness provenance" output: `results/provenance.json` includes suite id, git sha, dataset lockfile sha, tokenizer rev, CUDA/cuDNN, and runner image digest.
- Add docs for how to cut a new baseline (v2) without breaking comparability and how to reference the suite from perf-canary gating.

Artifact locations:
- Dataset bundle (read-only): `s3://redwood-benchmark-lab/datasets/runtime-lts/baseline/v1/` (populated by CI job `publish_lts_dataset_bundle`)
- Suite id: `runtime_lts_baseline_v1`

Notes/constraints:
- We intentionally avoid any new workloads that require gated/licensed corpora; v1 is built from existing internal benchmark content already used by perf-canary.
- Full benchmark runs remain too expensive for per-PR CI; this PR adds lightweight checksum/provenance verification + a tiny smoke run (1 model, 2 prompts) to ensure the suite is runnable.

Rollout plan:
- Land this PR.
- In perf-canary PR 311, switch LTS gating to reference `runtime_lts_baseline_v1` + `datasets/lts_baseline_v1.lock`.
- After first LTS RC, capture the provenance JSON as part of the audit evidence bundle.

Checklist:
- [x] Dataset lockfile includes SHA256 for each object
- [x] Bench runner fails closed on checksum mismatch
- [x] Suite definition pins seeds and prompt ordering
- [x] Provenance output includes dataset + harness identifiers
- [x] Docs explain baseline cut procedure + compatibility expectations
commits: datasets: introduce manifest + lockfile format and checksum verification
docs: add LTS baseline workflow and v2 cut instructions
ci: add publish job for dataset bundle + smoke validation
conversation:
Sean Gallagher (review): This is the missing piece for making the LTS perf gate defensible. Two asks: (1) ensure we pin tokenizer revision explicitly, not just whatever the model container includes; (2) make the runner fail closed if the lockfile is missing any referenced objects (right now it warns + continues).

Allison Grant (author): Good call. I added `tokenizer_rev` to provenance and to the suite yaml schema, and made `bench datasets fetch` error if any manifest entry is missing from the lockfile (or if extra objects appear). Updated docs to clarify that LTS suite must not run without a lockfile.

Kira Volkov (review): Can we make sure prompt ordering is deterministic even if manifests are regenerated? We should sort by `prompt_id` before sampling.

Allison Grant (author): Done. Manifests are still JSONL for readability, but we normalize into a sorted list by `prompt_id` before applying any sampling or sharding. Added a unit test that fails if order changes with identical inputs.

Sahana Iyer (review): For CI: the publish workflow should be restricted to main only, but we still need a PR check that verifies all hashes. Looks like you did a dry-run job—please confirm it doesn’t attempt S3 writes.

Allison Grant (author): Confirmed—PR path uses `--dry-run` and the workflow is `pull_request` scoped with no AWS creds. Main branch publish is `workflow_dispatch` + `push` on main only with OIDC role.

Hiro Tanaka (review): Any concerns about suite coverage for scheduler regressions (prefill vs decode)?

Allison Grant (author): v1 includes separate prefill-heavy and decode-heavy slices with pinned seq-lens and batch profiles; see suite yaml sections `profiles.prefill_focus` and `profiles.decode_focus`. If we need more coverage we’ll do it in v2; v1 is intended to be stable and minimal.

Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Please coordinate with perf-canary PR 311 to consume `runtime_lts_baseline_v1` and ensure provenance.json is attached to the RC evidence bundle.

Merge (squash) by Allison Grant after all checks passed.
